papers.title: An investigation of 6-DOF robot path planning using evolutionary algorithms
papers.summary: Multi-objective optimization (MOO) plays a vital role in robotics, where several conflicting objectives—such as minimizing energy consumption, execution time, and motion jerk—must be simultaneously satisfied. Traditional single-objective approaches fail to represent the trade-offs among such competing criteria, motivating the adoption of population-based evolutionary and swarm intelligence algorithms. papers.title: Substrate-dependent friction and climbing performance in a flying snake
papers.summary: Locomotion in limbless animals depends on friction between the body and substrate. In snakes, the skin-substrate interface can generate frictional anisotropy, lowering resistance during forward motion while increasing resistance during backward or transverse motion. These properties have inspired models and robots that rely on directional friction, yet empirical measurements remain limited across species and substrates. papers.title: A Robot Should Know When Its Bus Is Gone: A Conservative Dual-Route, Fault-Isolation State Machine for Modular Servo Systems
papers.summary: Low-cost modular robotic arms commonly share serial-bus and power dependencies. A broken connector or local overcurrent can leave an otherwise functional robot unable to complete an authorized task. This technical report presents a minimal, dry-run fault-isolation and alternate-route proposal engine for six simulated servo joints. It represents primary/backup connectivity, measured-current threshold, observation age, explicit owner authorization, and STOP epochs, and generates proposed routes without contacting servos. papers.summary: Participatory and deliberative democratic theories require citizens to exercise epistemic agency and cultivate epistemic virtues such as independent belief formation, willingness to revise one’s beliefs, and openness to listening to divergent perspectives. papers.summary: Understanding how birds encode object color is fundamental to elucidating the neural mechanisms of color vision. Although behavioral studies have shown high color-discrimination accuracy in birds, it remains unclear whether higher-order visual areas organize color information in a structured manner. papers.title: Object recognition from dynamic cues: Examining the inversion effect
papers.summary: Humans can identify and categorize objects in a dynamic visual scene with remarkable accuracy. To achieve this, our visual system relies not only on static information but also on dynamic cues. Turning a static image upside down hinders recognition. Similar inversion effects have been found in dynamic videos of human action. However, it is unknown whether this inversion effect extends to a broader set of categories when only dynamic cues are available. papers.title: SparseTG-GS: Test Case Generation via Sparse Perturbation Group
papers.summary: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have been widely applied in the field of computer vision. While DNNs exhibit remarkable accuracy in classification tasks, they remain susceptible to adversarial examples. Robustness testing for DNNs has become crucial. Existing test case generation methods suffer from certain limitations, such as dispersed distribution of perturbations, insufficient realism, and high time cost. papers.summary: This study addresses skill discontinuity in traditional embodied crafts, using Taiwanese pastry-mold craftsmanship as a case. papers.title: The use of cognitive bias modification to reduce body dissatisfaction: Manipulation of interpretation bias, perfectionism, and cognitive flexibility
papers.summary: The aim of this study is to experimentally manipulate interpretation bias, perfectionism, and cognitive flexibility using cognitive bias modification techniques and to understand which cognitive process, if not all, can reduce body dissatisfaction.

papers.title: Controlled flight of an insect-scale flapping-wing robot via integrated onboard sensing and computation
papers.summary: Aerial insects can effortlessly navigate dense vegetation, whereas similarly sized aerial robots typically depend on offboard sensors and computation to maintain stable flight. This disparity restricts insect-scale robots to operation in motion-capture environments, substantially limiting their applicability to tasks such as search-and-rescue operations and precision agriculture. In this work, we present a 1.29-gram aerial robot capable of hovering and tracking trajectories with solely onboard sensing and computation. papers.title: Manufacturing Dark Green Religion in the European Ecovillage Milieu
papers.summary: Ecovillages in Europe are places of embodied and performed dark green religion (DGR) where the gap between environmental values and behavior highlighted by Yi-Fu Tuan in 1970 may, at least in part, be narrowed. Ecovillages may also enable the human animal to better adapt to its habitats, in part due to DGR worldviews and the dwelling practices informed by various of its nature reverencing spiritualities. papers.title: The Effect of Perceptually Challenging Conditions on Speech and Sign Language Perception
papers.summary: Language is often processed in perceptually challenging conditions. Although the neural correlates of speech processing in such conditions have been well studied, this is not the case for sign language. Thus, it is unknown whether the neural mechanisms involved in this process are comparable across language modalities. One reason for the lack of studies in sign language might be attributed to the difficulties in adapting perceptual manipulations from the context of speech to sign language. papers.summary: Visual working memory (VWM) guides attention via internal attentional templates, but whether this relies on a "single" or "multiple" templates and how awareness and VWM load regulate its neural mechanisms remain unclear. This study used a VWM-guided visual search paradigm with backward masking (awareness manipulation) and EEG.
